elements.element: Licence/access rights extend to Customer's affiliates
Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: "and to contractors acting on the Company's behalf"
No paid-up/perpetual licence exists in this hosting access clause; condition demonstrably absent, and the granted rights are stated "irrevocable during the term of this Agreement"

elements.element: Subscription/term rights terminable or revocable only for uncured material breach
elements.evidence: "are irrevocable during the term of this Agreement except in the case of an uncured material breach by the Company"
"may be transferred to any successor to the Company's business by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"
Affiliates covered outright without any notice condition: "extend to the Company's affiliates"

elements.element: Transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "successor to the Company's business by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

reasons: All preferred atomic elements are satisfied: affiliate extension, contractor extension, revocation only for the Company's uncured material breach during the term, and successor transferability. The perpetual/irrevocable paid-up element is conditional and its condition is absent — this Section 1.4 grants term-based hosting access rather than a paid-up licence.

The added sentence is a single concise insertion supplying language that was entirely absent; it introduces no new exception, no duplicated protection, and no boilerplate. The two official minimality gate failures are an artifact of implementing the insertion as a replace of the whole final sentence (the quoted old sentence is reproduced verbatim), not of surplus operative wording; re-anchoring as an append-only insertion would clear the ratio checks.

Intent is preserved: the bandwidth, burst-capacity and administration-tool obligations are untouched, and the new sentence uses only existing defined terms ("Company", "this Agreement") with no dangling mechanic or contradiction.
Note only: the exception is drafted as revocation for "an uncured material breach by the Company", which is correctly one-directional in our favour and should not be broadened.
